`range(1, len(items))` starts at index 1, and Python lists are 0-indexed, so `items[0]` is never visited. *(fact)*

```python
for item in items:
    process(item)
```

If you need the index too, use `for i, item in enumerate(items): process(item)`, or `range(len(items))` if you must keep the index-based form. *(fact)*

If the skip was intentional (for example, `items[0]` is a header row), your original loop was correct. In that case `for item in items[1:]:` says so more clearly. *(heuristic)*
